examples.japanese: IT{企業|きぎょう}に{転職|てんしょく}した。
examples.english: I changed jobs to an IT company.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}サイトで{仕事|しごと}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for a job on a job-hunting site.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}を{考|かんが}えている。
{転職|てんしょく}{活動|かつどう}を{始|はじ}めたが、なかなか{良|よ}い{会社|かいしゃ}が{見|み}つからない。
examples.english: I started job hunting, but I can't seem to find a good company.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}して{給料|きゅうりょう}は{上|あ}がったが、{前|まえ}の{会社|かいしゃ}の{方|ほう}が{働|はたら}きやすかった。
examples.english: My salary went up after changing jobs, but my previous company was easier to work at.

notes:
{転職|てんしょく} means changing from one company to another. This is different from {転勤|てんきん}, which is a transfer within the same company.

Distinction:
- {転職|てんしょく}: changing companies
- {転勤|てんきん}: transferring within the same company

Common expressions:
- {転職|てんしょく}する (change jobs)
- {転職|てんしょく}{活動|かつどう} (job hunting activities)
- {転職|てんしょく}サイト / {転職|てんしょく}エージェント (job change website/agency)

Cultural note:
Job-hopping was traditionally viewed negatively in Japan, where lifetime employment was the norm. However, changing jobs has become more common and accepted in recent years.
